title: World, bodily nature, beginning (II.1–3)
english: Book II takes up the world properly: its beginning, end, and what providence dispenses between. Bodily nature’s persistence is discussed without making matter a second unbegotten principle. The world’s start and causes are read under one Creator.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 22 (1913) Rufinus Latin; disclose Rufinus paraphrase.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; no ANF Crombie / Butterworth.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
BOOK II start after Book I CLOSEOUT.

title: One God of law and prophets; just and good (II.4–5)
english: Against dividing gods: the God of the law and the prophets is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. “Just” and “good” are not two deities; Scripture’s severity and kindness meet in one will.

title: Incarnation, Spirit, soul, world-motions, resurrection — BOOK II CLOSEOUT
english: The Savior’s incarnation, the Spirit’s work, the soul, the motions of rational creatures, and resurrection-and-judgment are treated in order. Promises are not emptied into mere metaphor, nor is the resurrection made a crass flesh-only hope. BOOK II CLOSEOUT.
